clue.text: Given to eat chopped up greenstuff

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into bits, so these three words' letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a pile of chopped greens to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' tells you to rearrange the letters of GIVEN TO EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants in general, green leaves and growth, are collectively called vegetation.

clue.text: Line may be put in place

indicators.note: one word is put inside another, so the synonym for may goes into the synonym for place

parts.note: to place is to set down
may and can both express being allowed or able

explanation.surface: An instruction that a line may be put in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' looks like general text, but it is the geometric definition; 'put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a secant is a straight line cutting a curve at two or more points.

clue.text: Number accepting a post with new French leader

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it in, so the abbreviation for number holds the next pieces

parts.note: a pole is an upright post

explanation.surface: A count of people taking a mail job alongside a fresh head of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French leader' tempts you to take the first letter F; it is the whole definition, a famous ruler of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte, emperor of the French, is the obvious French leader of history.

clue.text: After which it is dipped in bleach

indicators.note: dipping one thing in another places it inside, so the word it goes into the synonym for after which

parts.note: when can mean 'after which', as in 'he left, when the trouble started'

explanation.surface: Instructions for laundry: something dipped in bleach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bleach' is the definition used as a verb, not the liquid in which something is dipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach cloth or teeth is to make them paler, a synonym verb.

indicators.note: something not exactly as written is changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is roughly as liable as a queen would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not exactly' tells you to rearrange LIABLE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Several queens bore this name, among them the Castilian monarch who backed Columbus.

clue.text: Doctor taking note of unhealthy atmosphere

parts.note: SMO, senior medical officer, is a doctor's title
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A physician remarks on the unwholesome air in a place.
explanation.walkthrough: SMO stands for senior medical officer; 'taking' simply joins it to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog over a city is an unwholesome kind of air.

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the synonym for chance is read by its sound

parts.note: fate means chance or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone learns of an opportunity to party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard of' says FATE, said out loud, gives the spelling FETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a festival or outdoor fair held to celebrate or raise money.

clue.text: Still can't tell one from another

explanation.surface: A person still unable to distinguish between things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless (still) and also identical, so indistinguishable.

parts.note: reads as someone only mildly keen on theft, but describes a thief whose hands are deft and deftly nimble

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a moderate thief; the phrase meant is one for a pickpocket, read as fingers that are not heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket with nimble, deft hands is described with this phrase for thievish.

explanation.surface: Coping and departing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to cope (manage) and to leave, as in 'I must be off'.

clue.text: Also about to seize West Indian island

indicators.note: one word goes about another, surrounding it, so the synonym for also wraps the next

parts.note: too means also
to bag is to seize or catch

explanation.surface: Someone is also about to capture a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'to' is only a link; 'West' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the smaller partner of Trinidad in a Caribbean nation.

explanation.surface: Hold on to a piece on the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is a fortified tower, and the rook on a chessboard is also called by this name.

parts.note: reads as a person of unsound morals, but means a voice or noise with no quality of tone

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound character' looks like moral soundness; it means the timbre of a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, expressionless voice has no tone, so it is described this way.

parts.note: reads as writing paper, but means paper printed with musical notes

explanation.walkthrough: Note-paper normally means writing paper; here the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed scores of musical notes on paper are called by this name.

clue.text: Sort of snide reaction that's thoughtless

indicators.note: to sort something is to arrange it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cutting reply that shows a lack of care for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' tells you to rearrange SNIDE REACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heedless of others' feelings is uncaring and thoughtless.

indicators.note: a drunken person reels about, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is not a letter, so the word supplies CANT

explanation.surface: A tipsy rake finds himself unable to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges ROUE and CANT; a roue is a debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: A courante is an old French court dance in triple time.

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: something replaced is put back differently, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A former European court has been superseded by a trustee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' asks for the letters of the word court to be rearranged, not for a court to be superseded.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who carries out a will is entrusted with the estate.

clue.text: Quarters in the course of becoming permanent

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are two quarters of the compass
during means in the course of

explanation.surface: Lodgings in the middle of a process turning permanent.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are called quarters, so 'Quarters' gives E and N; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting a long time is lasting or permanent.

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means upset or flustered (a state) and partly or somewhat.

clue.text: Provoke many to leave around the end of June

indicators.note: to leave is placed around the word for many, enclosing it

parts.note: to exit is to leave
C is a hundred in Roman numerals, standing for many

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here taken from June

explanation.surface: Something stirs up many people to go away at the close of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside EXIT, and 'the end of' June adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite feelings is to stir them up or provoke them.

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
here means at this point

explanation.surface: Someone holds steady at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick together is to hold fast as one, a synonym.

indicators.note: the letters come from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An animal native to the Antiguan islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters inside ANTIGUAN ARCHIPELAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical lizard is a creature.

clue.text: Scot's' girl by the sound of it

indicators.note: points to a word spoken, so the girl's name is read by its sound

parts.note: Gail is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's lass is mentioned, judging by the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' says GAIL, spoken, gives the spelling GAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland Scot speaking or descended from Gaelic speakers is a Gael.

parts.note: a rough surface is not even
a book or record that is out has been released and is on sale

explanation.surface: A drawing that is uneven is on the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough out a plan is to draft it loosely, to sketch it.

clue.text: Novel place on the North Devon coast

definitions.text: place on the North Devon coast

explanation.surface: A book and a seaside spot in North Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the village takes its name from Charles Kingsley's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley's 1855 adventure book shares its title with a seaside village founded later.

indicators.note: something returned goes back, so the synonym for story-teller is read backwards

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untruths

explanation.surface: A narrator comes back to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story-teller' means a liar rather than an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a bar, as a towel bar or handrail.
